ac_143_1_measurement.actual_mechanism: OCCLUSION BY AN ADJACENT PANE. The stack dump at the click point (444.4, 285.5) returned journal-next-day (433.72..455.09) AND pane-b (444.0..660.0) AND editor.rich.text (444.0..660.0). pane-a, which owns the journal editor, spans x 228.0..444.0. The date-nav row overflowed it: journal-next-day 433.7..455.1 (half outside), journal-calendar-toggle 463.1..484.5 and journal-today 492.5..535.6 (both ENTIRELY outside). egui_kittest and canonical Argus dispatch a click at the node rect CENTRE, so the click landed on pane-b's rich-text editor. The navigation therefore never ran, which is why no PUT /loom/journals/<second_date> and no second-date calendar GET ever reached the mock server.
ac_143_1_measurement.root_cause: The date display is unbounded content laid out BEFORE the trailing controls, so it consumed the row width and pushed the buttons past the pane's right edge. Identical class to the MT-119 saved-search row and the MT-122 result-row badge.

scope.summary: A mounted next-day click on the daily-journal surface must actually navigate while a calendar read for the previous date is still in flight. Today it does not. test_calendar_interop::mounted_navigation_while_old_get_is_in_flight_cancels_without_fr_residue clicks the journal-EDITOR next-day control (author_id `journal-next-day`, JOURNAL_DATE_NAV_AUTHOR_IDS, rendered by rich_editor/daily_notes/journal_panel.rs line 439) and then waits for the MOUNTED graph::daily_journal_panel::DailyJournalState to reach the second date with projection NoEvent. It never does. The mock request log captured at the failure shows only first-date traffic after the click: GET /knowledge/documents, POST /loom/search-v2, PUT /loom/journals/<first_date>, GET /api/flight_recorder, and the /calendar/events GET for <first_date> twice. There is no PUT /loom/journals/<second_date> and no /calendar/events GET for <second_date>. Because the editor's own handler (journal_panel.rs, DateNavOutcome::Navigated -> state.store.open(date)) would itself have issued that PUT, the editor's nav did not advance either. The click is therefore NOT landing on the control at all, rather than landing and being dropped downstream. Two mechanisms remain open and must be distinguished by measurement before any fix: (a) POSITION drift, since egui_kittest dispatches a click at the observed node's rect and the conditional projection labels in graph/daily_journal_panel.rs ('Loading calendar event and activity...', 'Waiting for daily note...', 'Calendar binding paused...') appear and disappear as the transient read settles, moving every widget below them between the inspected frame and the frame that processes the click; (b) IDENTITY drift of an ANCESTOR of the nav row, the same class MT-113 and MT-117 hit. Stabilizing the DateNavWidget row itself was already attempted and did NOT change the outcome, and that attempt was reverted, so the row's own scope is not the cause. This microtask must also decide and record whether the mounted daily-journal panel is expected to follow the EDITOR's date navigation at all: the editor nav writes only the editor's own DateNav and store, while the mounted panel's nav advances only through DailyJournalEvent::DateNavigated emitted by the panel's own widget (author_ids DAILY_JOURNAL_DATE_NAV_AUTHOR_IDS, graph/daily_journal_panel.rs line 563). If no such cross-surface sync is intended, then the product contract is what needs stating and the test must be corrected to the surface that owns the state it asserts on, with the reasoning recorded rather than the assertion weakened.
scope.embedded_mode_boundary: Frontend-only. This microtask must not add, restore, or depend on SQLite or PostgreSQL, and must not change backend storage. The Calendar reads under test are served by the test's transient mock server, not by a real backend.
acceptance_criteria: AC-143-1: the mechanism is MEASURED before it is fixed. A fix landed without that measurement does not satisfy this microtask; this is the exact discipline that closed MT-113.

AC-143-2: after the change, a mounted next-day click issued while a calendar read for the previous date is still in flight results in the navigation actually taking effect on the surface that owns the clicked control, proven by the product issuing the second date's request rather than by a UI assertion alone.

AC-143-3: the cross-surface question is answered explicitly, both in this contract and in the in-product UserManual where it is operator- or model-visible: either the mounted daily-journal panel follows the editor's date navigation (and that wiring exists and is tested), or it does not (and the test asserts against the surface that owns the state).
